item.text:
Deep-sea mining cannot be guaranteed to end battery-metal shortages. Here’s strong advocacy copy without that unsupported promise.

### (a) Three posts under 280 characters

1. We back commercial deep-sea mining to expand battery-metal supplies. We need more sources of the materials that power electrification—and we want deep-sea resources to be part of that supply.

2. We want a stronger battery-metal supply chain. Commercial deep-sea mining belongs in that strategy: another source of essential materials, alongside recycling and land-based production.

3. We support opening a new source of battery metals through commercial deep-sea mining. We’re pushing for a broader supply base that supports electrification and reduces dependence on existing sources.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 107 words

We support commercial deep-sea mining because we want a broader, stronger supply of the metals that power batteries. We cannot build an electrified future without securing the materials it requires. We see deep-sea resources as an important addition to that supply, alongside land-based mining and recycling. Our position is clear: we should develop this new source rather than leave it out of our strategy. We also insist on rigorous environmental standards, transparent oversight and accountability. We want a battery-metal supply chain built for growing demand, and we are making the case for commercial deep-sea mining to take its place in that effort.
